title: Attorney General of Idaho

context.text: Neither major-party primary was contested: incumbent Raúl Labrador (R) advanced unopposed with 186,106 votes and Lori Hickman (D) advanced unopposed with 44,212 votes on May 19, 2026.
The Idaho Capital Sun reports that Labrador and Hickman will be on the Nov. 3 ballot; The Green Papers lists only the two.

candidates.name: Raúl Labrador
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the May 19 Republican primary.

summary.text: Raúl Labrador is Idaho's Republican Attorney General, seeking a second term. A former immigration attorney, he served in the Idaho House and in the U.S. House representing Idaho's 1st District from 2011 to 2019 before taking office as Attorney General in 2023.

background.text: Born in Carolina, Puerto Rico; earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University (1992) and a law degree from the University of Washington (1995).
Served in the Idaho House of Representatives (2006-2010) and the U.S. House of Representatives (2011-2019).

priorities.text: Defending parental rights, citing cases where he led coalitions of states defending the constitutional rights of parents.
Protecting Idaho children from technology companies, including a consumer-protection lawsuit against OpenAI.
Defending the Second Amendment, citing Idaho's multistate suit that led to the ATF ending enforcement of registration for suppressors and short-barreled rifles.

statements.quote: For more than 90 years, the federal government made law-abiding citizens ask permission, pay a tax, and wait months to exercise their constitutional rights. Idaho sued, Idaho won
statements.context: On the ATF's October 2026 guidance on suppressors and short-barreled rifles.

record.text: Announced a lawsuit against OpenAI in Idaho's Fourth Judicial District Court under the Idaho Consumer Protection Act over alleged harms to children and deception of parents.
Announced that a court victory Idaho won with 14 other states led the ATF to stop enforcing registration, wait and tax requirements for suppressors, short-barreled rifles and short-barreled shotguns.
Won dismissal in federal court of Le Soleil Child Care v. Labrador, a challenge to the Idaho Medical Freedom Act.

Led a coalition of 18 states, Puerto Rico and the Arizona Legislature in filing an amicus brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to hear Detwiler v. Mid-Columbia Medical Center, a religious-accommodation case.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site (raullabrador.com) has little text beyond a donation page, so priorities are taken from his office's releases and newsletter. No direct statement mapping to an issue statement other than the quoted one was found.

candidates.name: Lori Hickman
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the May 19 Democratic primary.

summary.text: Lori Hickman is the Democratic nominee for Attorney General. An Idaho attorney with more than 20 years of experience, she has worked in private practice, as in-house counsel at Micron Technology and as a clerk for the U.S. District Court of Idaho.

background.text: Graduated from Borah High School; earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University (1988) and a law degree from BYU's J. Reuben Clark Law School (1991).
Practiced at firms of various sizes, including a New York City firm, served as in-house counsel at Micron Technology, and clerked for the U.S. District Court for the District of Idaho.
Provides pro bono counsel to guardians ad litem in child-protection cases.

priorities.text: Restore trust and integrity to the Attorney General's office, saying the office should give sound legal advice 'based on the rule of law' and not be shaped by politics.
Provide prompt, accurate legal opinions to legislators and state officials, and highlight legal weaknesses that invite costly court challenges.
Act as 'the people's lawyer': protect consumers, keep communities safe, and defend the Constitution.

candidates.researchNotes: Not an officeholder, so no record. On abortion her campaign site says she would 'defend the constitutional right of the people to create the law'; that does not map to an issue statement in the guide.
